findings.claim: oneLine re-encodes every invalid UTF-8 byte of an error text as U+FFFD. An error that names a path holding non-UTF-8 bytes (for example a Latin-1 file name under the results or wiki directory) is now printed on stderr with those bytes replaced, so the printed path no longer matches the file on disk. Before this change the text was printed byte for byte with %v. Iterating over bytes, or copying invalid sequences through unchanged, would keep the original bytes and still make line breaks into spaces.
evidence: Diff lines 42-51: `for _, r := range text { ... b.WriteRune(r) }`. In Go, ranging over a string gives utf8.RuneError (U+FFFD) for each invalid byte, and WriteRune writes it as EF BF BD, so the original byte is lost.
Diff lines 21-22 and 28-29: the base printed `%v` of err/r verbatim; this commit sends both print sites through oneLine, so the replacement starts with this commit.
TestOneLineJoinsTheLinesOfAText (diff lines 104-121) covers only ASCII inputs, so nothing tests that bytes are kept.
